[](https://t.me/snowdensay) [](/grfdsasdvef/awesomeebpflinuxtracing/blob/main/LICENSE) [](/grfdsasdvef/awesomeebpflinuxtracing/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) 🚀 Snowden SAY Deep Systems Engineering Lab Community:Ежедневные глубокие разборы аварий на проде, memory leaks, тюнинг Linux kernel и lockfree паттерны — в нашем инженерном канале: [@snowdensay](https://t.me/snowdensay). 📚 Полная монография (все 5 глав + репозиторий с тестами): доступна в Telegramботе [@Snowden\_book\_bot](https://t.me/Snowden%5Fbook%5Fbot?start=ebpflinuxkernelperformanceobservability) 📑 Complete Curriculum Overview Module 1 (Included Below): Architectural Foundations, Memory Layouts & Invariants Module 2: HighConcurrency Core & LockFree Data Structures _(Full Handbook)_ Module 3: Production Crash Recovery, WAL & State Machine Consistency _(Full Handbook)_ Module 4: KernelBypass I/O, SIMD Acceleration & Hardware Offloading _(Full Handbook)_ Module 5: Live Incident PostMortems, Chaos Engineering & Production Benchmarks _(Full Handbook)_ Chapter 1 — eBPF Verifier Invariants: Memory Safety, BPF Maps, and Tail Calls in C & Rust 1.1 Verifier Architectural Model The verifier (kernel/bpf/verifier.c, \~14k lines as of 6.9) performs a symbolic execution of the entire instruction graph before any JIT compilation. It is a static analysis pass that must provably terminate and provably uphold four invariants per instruction: 1. C1 — DAG termination: No unbounded loops. Enforced via CFG backedge detection; the only sanctioned cycle is bpf_loop() (kernel ≥ 5.17) with a runtime callback whose iteration count is bounded at verification time. Legacy bounded loops (kernel ≥ 5.3) are unrolled — a loop with MAYBE\wide trip count N expands the explored state space by N. 2. C2 — Instruction budget: BPF_COMPLEXITY_LIMIT_INSNS = 1,000,000 (6.x; 128k hard cap pre5.2 with BPF_MAXINSNS = 4096 per program for nonprivileged). The verifier explores _paths_, not instructions — worst case state explosion is O(branches^depth), and a 4kinstruction program with datadependent branches can exhaust 1M processed instructions in \~60ms on a Zen 3. 3. C3 — Register state soundness: Every register carries a struct bpf_reg_state with a type (SCALAR_VALUE, PTR_TO_MAP_VALUE, PTR_TO_BTF_ID, PTR_TO_STACK, …), a tnum (trackednumbers abstraction: maskvalue bitpair encoding), and 32/64bit ranges. Precision analysis (kernel ≥ 5.4) does backpropagation to prune imprecise branches that would otherwise fork the state tree. 4. C4 — Memory safety: Every load/store must resolve to a statically known region with bounds proven by the tnum/range lattice. No speculative dereferences; no pointers leak to userspace unless scalarized through bpf_ktime\safe operations. flowchart TD A[bpf syscall BPF_PROG_LOAD] B[ELF/insn sanity: bpf_check size, opcode whitelist] B C[CFG construction + backedge detection] C cycle w/o bpf_loop X1[ELOOP rejected] C D[Depthfirst symbolic walk<br/bpf_verifier_env: 1M insn budget] D budget exhausted X2[E2BIG / EAGAIN] D E[perstate: reg bounds refine, ptr arithmetic check] E OOB access / ptr leak X3[EACCES] E F{state in explored_states hash?} F equivalent state cached D F G[fn exit: liveness pass, precision backprop] G H[JIT compile: x8664/ARM64, lockless text patching] H I[bpf_prog struct: 1 refcount, percpu stats, kallsyms entry] Loading Cost model (empirical, kernel 6.8, EPYC 7B13, vmstat\quiet host): Program class insns verifier wall time states explored peak verifier RSS XDP drop/firewall 120 0.9 ms 210 3.1 MB Cilium L3/L4 policy 2,850 14 ms 6,400 22 MB L7 HTTP parser (unrolled loops) 3,900 210 ms 148,000 310 MB Same L7 with bpf\_loop 1,100 26 ms 9,800 41 MB State explosion is the dominant cost. The explored_states hash (bpf_verifier_state_list, htab with jhash over register checksums) caches visited (insn_idx, branch_pred) states; a cache hit prunes the subtree. Precision loss — e.g., a scalar whose tnum mask covers 12 unknown low bits — defeats the cache because the checksum differs, and reexplores identical paths. Diagnose with BPF_LOG_LEVEL=2 equivalent: strace e bpf plus bpftool prog load with log_level=2, count from ... to: safe lines; 50k safelines signals cache thrash. 1.2 Invariant C4 Mechanics: Pointer Arithmetic Lattice

items.title: Show HN: HookArmor – Self-hosted webhook queue that defeats 300s replay expiry
items.desc: description: Zeroloss Webhook DeadLetter Queue (DLQ), sub10ms ingress buffer, automatic HMAC signature resigning, and 1click replay gateway for Stripe, Shopify, Clerk, and B2B SaaS. title: HookArmor — ZeroLoss Webhook Infrastructure & DeadLetter Replay Proxy image: https://hookarmour.dev/ogpreview.png MIT Open Source · SQLite WAL Fsync · Node 20+ · Zero Brokers Zeroloss webhook delivery. Built for Stripe & Shopify spikes. Deploy reboots, serverless cold starts, and DB pool exhaustion silently drop revenue webhooks. HookArmor buffers ingress in SQLite WAL under 10ms, absorbs failures for up to \~96 hours, and automatically resigns stale signatures on replay. npx docker local tunnel npm v1.4.6 · 119 tests passing $npx hookarmor start Copy Request Beta Access Added to HookArmor Cloud Beta Your address is queued. Want to run HookArmor right now? Launch locally in one command or inspect the codebase on GitHub. [View Repository](https://github.com/pkdoddamani/hookarmor) [Open Dashboard](/dashboard) [Download Free on GitHub](https://github.com/pkdoddamani/hookarmor) [Explore Architecture](architecture) hookarmortrace · POST /in/stripebilling 502 Deploy Reboot 504 DB Timeout 300s Replay Trap Captured Inbound Request Stored Bytes + Original Sig ReSigned Outbound Replay Fresh HMAC · Zero Code Change Verified Ingestion & ReSigning StripeSignature Shopify HMAC Clerk / Svix GitHub SHA256 Razorpay HMAC Mode B Internal Sig Prometheus /metrics Architecture Singlenode reliability without distributed queue sprawl No Kafka clusters, Redis brokers, or SQS deadletter race conditions. One selfcontained proxy backed by crashsafe SQLite WAL commits. EXTERNAL PROVIDERS Stripe · Shopify Clerk / GitHub / Razorpay POST /in/:endpointId HOOKARMOR INGRESS EDGE Verify HMAC + WAL Fsync AES256GCM secrets & body at rest Idempotency + bodyhash dedupe 200 OK ACK (<10ms) RELAY & GUARD ReSign & Pool HTTP KeepAlive sockets IPv4/IPv6 SSRF + DNS guard Fresh t=now HMAC header YOUR BACKEND App Handler Zero code changes /api/webhooks 5xx / 429 / Timeout DEADLETTER QUEUE & RETRY WORKER 10attempt schedule (\~96h) · Sentinel alerts · 1click UI & CLI bulk replay (up to 5k/batch) KeepAlive Ingress (<10ms) Returns an instant 200 OK once durable WAL synchronous=FULL fsync succeeds, while pooling persistent HTTP/HTTPS sockets downstream. \~96h Delivery Budget (10 Attempts) Outlasts Stripe's 3day retry schedule with jittered backoff (30s to 48h), plus instant local startup crash recovery and claim leases. ExpirationDefeating ReSigning Resigns outbound Stripe and Svix timestamps at t=now and supports up to 5,000\event CLI or UI replays with forensic provenance headers. AES256GCM & Compliance Mode Encrypts signing secrets, headers, and bodies at rest. Enable HOOKARMOR_REQUIRE_SECRETS to forbid unverified endpoints plus full IPv4/IPv6 SSRF blocking. Sentinel & Rejection Alerts Tracks failing streaks and ingress rejections (rotated secrets or scheme mismatches) with throttled Slack/Discord webhooks and Prometheus /metrics. Online Backups & Dev Tunneling Stream zerodowntime SQLite snapshots with hookarmor backup or tunnel live signed payloads straight into localhost:3000 in one terminal command. Integration Dropin compatibility or isolated internal verification Choose transparent resigning to leave existing Stripe handlers untouched, or isolate external provider secrets completely at the HookArmor edge. Mode A · Transparent Proxy (Default) HookArmor resigns outbound payloads with fresh t=now timestamps. Zero SDK rewrite required. Mode B · Isolated Trust Boundary Downstream handlers verify xhookarmorsignature using HOOKARMOR\_SIGNING\_SECRET only. routes/webhooks.js Copy Tradeoffs & Fit Designed against the alternatives Keep full custody of customer payment payloads in a single <50MB container without paying perevent SaaS markups. Você concentra os gastos no cartão para acumular milhas e cashback; nossa IA lê o PDF da fatura, separa o que é seu, o que é da casa e o que é de cada familiar, e já gera o QR Code Pix exato. [NubankPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/nubank)[ItaúPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/itau)[Banco InterPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/inter)[BradescoPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/bradesco)[SantanderPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/santander)[C6 BankPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/c6bank)[Banco do BrasilPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/bancodobrasil)[XPPDF suportado](/ferramentas/converterfaturapdfexcel/xp) Zero acesso às suas senhas bancárias Você nunca informa login, senha ou token do banco. Toda a importação acontece apenas pelo arquivo PDF da fatura. Extração híbrida com IA e conciliação Lê compras à vista, parceladas, cartões adicionais, créditos e descontos batendo com o valor oficial da fatura. Múltiplos cartões no mesmo fechamento Importe a fatura do Nubank e a do Itaú no mesmo mês e gere um único Pix consolidado para cada familiar pagar. Como funciona o Fattura em 3 passos Transforme horas de conferência manual em um fechamento tranquilo de 2 minutos. PASSO 01 Suba o PDF da fatura do banco Envie o PDF original do seu banco. O Fattura extrai todas as compras, identifica parcelas e já separa os gastos de cartões adicionais. PASSO 02 Atribua ou deixe cada familiar marcar Selecione várias compras de uma vez para atribuir a alguém, divida gastos da casa proporcionalmente ou convide a família para marcar. PASSO 03 Receba via QR Code Pix e acompanhe Envie o resumo pronto no WhatsApp. Cada pessoa paga pelo QR Code Pix ou Copia e Cola e informa o pagamento no painel. O fim do estresse mensal Por que trocar a calculadora e a planilha pelo Fattura Veja a diferença entre fechar a fatura no braço e deixar a inteligência artificial organizar tudo. Como a maioria sofre todo mês ✕Conferência manual linha por linha: abrir um PDF de 8 páginas e somar 90 compras na calculadora do celular tentando não errar nenhum número. ✕Nomes indecifráveis na fatura: ninguém lembra o que foi PGMERCADOPAGO no dia 12 às 21h. ✕Parcelas esquecidas no meio do caminho: você lembra de cobrar a parcela 1/10 do parente, mas esquece de cobrar a 4/10 e paga do próprio bolso. ✕Desgaste para cobrar no WhatsApp: mandar prints riscados e ficar perguntando se a pessoa já fez o Pix. Como fica com o Fattura Leitura instantânea e conciliada: arraste o PDF e veja todas as compras, estornos e descontos baterem centavo por centavo com o total do banco. Cartão adicional reconhecido sozinho: identifica os portadores dos cartões adicionais e já sugere a conta do familiar correspondente. Memória inteligente de parcelas: se o seu irmão assumiu a parcela 1/10, o Fattura já atribui a 2/10 para ele no mês seguinte. Pix Copia e Cola + QR Code na tela: cada membro vê seu extrato transparente, escaneia o QR Code pelo computador ou copia o Pix exato no celular. Tecnologia pensada para famílias Tudo o que sua casa precisa para ter paz financeira Cada detalhe foi desenhado para eliminar o trabalho braçal de quem empresta ou divide o cartão. Precisão contábil e cartões adicionais Bate centavo por centavo com o PDF e separa cada portador Nosso motor híbrido soma compras, estornos e descontos na fatura para garantir que o valor extraído seja exatamente igual ao total cobrado pelo banco — já etiquetando quem usou cartão adicional. [](https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/OgnjenAdzic28/hush) hushlaunch.mp4 Hush lets any agent see and drive the apps on your computer, in the background, while you keep working. Read a window, click, type, read it again: 178 ms. The next fastest tool takes 653 ms. That's fast enough to win oneminute bullet against a 2200 chess.com bot, to play the third movement of the Moonlight Sonata at full tempo with every note on time, and to run ten agents on ten apps at once on one machine, all without anything coming to the front. How it compares Same window, same machine, one round of read, click, type, read ([details](/OgnjenAdzic28/hush/blob/main/docs/comparison.md)): Tool Round Works hidden Works on another Space Tool list (MCP) Hush 178 ms yes yes 972 tokens[1](usercontentfntoolsef23982d0659a39a8305e791d5adb836) agentdesktop 653 ms yes no 10,514 tokens cuadriver 1,134 ms yes mostly 50,397 tokens Peekaboo 3,506 ms no no 13,847 tokens opencomputeruse 4,297 ms yes yes 2,654 tokens On [Cua Driver Bench v2](/OgnjenAdzic28/hush/blob/main/docs/benchmark.md)'s background tasks, agents on Hush went 15/15 with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and with Claude Haiku 5.5, the user never disturbed once. Sonnet took a median 17.8 s per task.
